issue_title: Celery Beat: daily relative schedules become immediately due across DST fall-back
issue_body:
# Checklist - [x] I have verified that the issue exists against the `main` branch of Celery. - [ ] This has already been asked to the [discussions forum](https://github.com/celery/celery/discussions) first. - [x] I have read the relevant section in the [contribution guide](https://docs.celeryq.dev/en/main/contributing.html#other-bugs) on reporting bugs. - [x] I have checked the [issues list](https://github.com/celery/celery/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3A%22Issue+Type%3A+Bug+Report%22+-label%3A%22Category%3A+Documentation%22) for similar or identical bug reports. - [x] I have checked the [pull requests list](https://github.com/celery/celery/pulls?q=is%3Apr+label%3A%22PR+Type%3A+Bugfix%22+-label%3A%22Category%3A+Documentation%22) for existing proposed fixes. - [x] I have checked the [commit log](https://github.com/celery/celery/commits/main) to find out if the bug was already fixed in the main branch. - [x] I have included all related issues and possible duplicate issues in this issue (If there are none, check this box anyway). - [ ] I have tried to reproduce the issue with [pytest-celery](https://docs.celeryq.dev/projects/pytest-celery/en/latest/userguide/celery-bug-report.html) and added the reproduction script below. Discussion posting and pytest-celery reproduction have not been performed. The standalone test below exercises the scheduling calculation directly; no running broker, backend, worker, or Beat process is required. ## Mandatory Debugging Information - [x] I have included the output of ``celery -A proj report`` in the issue. (if you are not able to do this, then at least specify the Celery version affected). - [x] I have verified that the issue exists against the `main` branch of Celery. - [x] I have included the contents of ``pip freeze`` in the issue. - [x] I have included all the versions of all the external dependencies required to reproduce this bug. ## Optional Debugging Information - [x] I have tried reproducing the issue on more than one Python version and/or implementation. - [ ] I have tried reproducing the issue on more than one message broker and/or result backend. - [ ] I have tried reproducing the issue on more than one version of the message broker and/or result backend. - [ ] I have tried reproducing the issue on more than one operating system. - [ ] I have tried reproducing the issue on more than one workers pool. - [ ] I have tried reproducing the issue with autoscaling, retries, ETA/Countdown & rate limits disabled. - [ ] I have tried reproducing the issue after downgrading and/or upgrading Celery and its dependencies. ## Related Issues and Possible Duplicates #### Related Issues - [PR #10769](https://github.com/celery/celery/pull/10769) introduced elapsed-time interval addition. Combining that addition with daily relative rounding causes this regression. The [review](https://github.com/celery/celery/pull/10769#pullrequestreview-5406888408) also raised concerns about `relative=True` and `delta_resolution()`. - [PR #10813](https://github.com/celery/celery/pull/10813) addresses elapsed-time subtraction for ETA/countdown and expiry; it does not fix this Beat deadline calculation. - [Issue #6438](https://github.com/celery/celery/issues/6438) concerns interval scheduling at DST fall-back and was addressed by #10769. - [PR #4403](https://github.com/celery/celery/pull/4403) and [issue #1604](https://github.com/celery/celery/issues/1604) concern DST/crontab behavior rather than this daily interval regression. - [PR #7901](https://github.com/celery/celery/pull/7901) is an earlier DST-related scheduling proposal; [#7125](https://github.com/celery/celery/pull/7125) discusses a broader next-scheduled-time API. #### Possible Duplicates - No exact issue, PR, or discussion was found for this regression in the repository searches. Related DST reports are listed above. ## Environment & Settings **Celery version**: `5.7.0b1`, imported from the unchanged `main` source at [`71d1b8f89d50694ad2774ee2dcf3204dd2ae5272`](https://github.com/celery/celery/commit/71d1b8f89d50694ad2774ee2dcf3204dd2ae5272). Reproduced on CPython 3.12.3 and 3.11.16, on Linux/WSL2. The affected `celery/utils/time.py` blob is `e54b29b5d6b7dfff6f75f41473d9f460ed8ffd66`. The environment's installed distribution metadata reports `celery==5.6.3` in `pip freeze`. The reproduction explicitly imports the unchanged main checkout through `PYTHONPATH`; `celery.__version__` and the report below therefore show the source version, `5.7.0b1`. The configuration used by `celery -A proj report` is: ```python from celery import Celery app = Celery('dst_repro', broker='memory://', backend='cache+memory://') app.conf.timezone = 'America/New_York' ```

# Steps to Reproduce 1. Use the unchanged Celery main revision linked above. The local fix is not required for reproduction. 2. Save the minimally reproducible test below as `repro.py` outside the checkout. 3. Run `PYTHONPATH=/path/to/unchanged-celery-checkout python repro.py` with Celery's dependencies installed. 4. Observe a negative remaining duration and `is_due=True`, despite the previous run occurring at the current time. The example fixes the clock explicitly; do not change the system clock. ## Required Dependencies - **Minimal Python Version**: Unknown; reproduced on CPython 3.11.16 and 3.12.3 - **Minimal Celery Version**: Unknown release; regression introduced by #10769, reproduced on main (`5.7.0b1`) - **Minimal Kombu Version**: Unknown; environment uses `5.7.0a1` - **Minimal Broker Version**: N/A; no running broker is needed - **Minimal Result Backend Version**: N/A; no running result backend is needed - **Minimal OS and/or Kernel Version**: Unknown; reproduced on Linux/WSL2, kernel `6.18.40.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2` - **Minimal Broker Client Version**: N/A; no broker operations are involved - **Minimal Result Backend Client Version**: N/A; no backend operations are involved ### Python Packages

### Other Dependencies

- IANA timezone data must contain `America/New_York`. The environment uses system zoneinfo data and has `tzdata==2026.4` installed. - `tzlocal==5.4.4`, `billiard==4.3.0`, `vine==5.1.0`, `python-dateutil==2.9.0.post0`, and other installed versions are listed above. - The configured in-memory broker/backend are only used to construct the app and produce diagnostics. No external services or daemon logs are needed.

## Minimally Reproducible Test Case

```python from datetime import datetime, timedelta from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo from celery import Celery from celery.schedules import schedule app = Celery('dst_repro', broker='memory://', backend='cache+memory://') app.conf.timezone = 'America/New_York' last_run_at = datetime(2026, 11, 1, 0, 30, tzinfo=ZoneInfo('America/New_York')) s = schedule( timedelta(days=1), relative=True, nowfun=lambda: last_run_at, app=app, ) print('remaining:', s.remaining_estimate(last_run_at)) print('is_due:', s.is_due(last_run_at)) assert s.remaining_estimate(last_run_at) == timedelta(seconds=88200) assert s.is_due(last_run_at) == (False, 88200) ```

# Expected Behavior For `relative=True` and `timedelta(days=1)`, advance by one local calendar day and then round to midnight. A previous run at `2026-11-01 00:30 EDT` should have its next deadline at `2026-11-02 00:00 EST`. At `now == last_run_at`, the expected result is: ```text remaining: 1 day, 0:30:00 is_due: schedstate(is_due=False, next=88200.0) ``` The 88,200 seconds include the extra hour introduced by the DST rollback. # Actual Behavior On unchanged main, the test produces: ```text remaining: -1 day, 23:30:00 is_due: schedstate(is_due=True, next=86400.0) ``` The included assertion fails: ```text Traceback (most recent call last): File "repro.py", line 16, in assert s.remaining_estimate(last_run_at) == timedelta(seconds=88200) AssertionError ``` The calculation adds 86,400 elapsed seconds, reaching `2026-11-01 23:30 EST`, then `delta_resolution()` rounds that down to `2026-11-01 00:00 EDT`. This deadline is 1,800 seconds before `last_run_at`, so `schedule.is_due()` considers the task immediately due. Beat can dispatch additional runs on consecutive ticks before the deadline advances. Related cases also fail: two-day relative intervals across DST, daily relative intervals around spring-forward that round to the following date instead of the intended date, and hourly relative schedules during Lord Howe's half-hour rollback. Hourly schedules during a full repeated hour must retain elapsed-time arithmetic so both occurrences can execute. Suggested fix in PR #10818
